summary: Crash when set_ominous_bottle_amplifier item modifier sets out-of-range amplifier
description: Summary This is yet another "item modifier setting invalid component causing crash" bug. Here, the new set_ominous_bottle_amplifier item modifier does not clamp or validate the amplifier, causing a crash. Steps to Reproduce - Give yourself a stick. - Run the following command: item modify entity s hotbar.0 {function:"set_ominous_bottle_amplifier",amplifier:10} - Pause the game. Expected Result The game does not crash. Actual Result The game crashes.
Steps to Reproduce:
1. Create a new Creative world with default settings.
2. Give yourself a stick using the command `/give s stick`.
3. Run the following command: `item modify entity s hotbar.0 {function:"set_ominous_bottle_amplifier",amplifier:10}`.
4. Pause the game.
5. Observe that the game crashes.
Environment: Minecraft Java Edition Versions: 24w13a, 1.20.5 Pre-Release 1 (includes snapshots)
Observed Behavior:
### Actual Result

When attempting to set an out-of-range amplifier value using the `set_ominous_bottle_amplifier` item modifier, the game crashes immediately upon pausing. Specifically, running the command `item modify entity @s hotbar.0 {function:"set_ominous_bottle_amplifier",amplifier:10}` on a stick causes an out-of-bounds error due to the amplifier value not being validated or clamped within acceptable limits. This results in the game engine failing to handle the invalid input, leading to a complete crash of the Minecraft client.
Expected Behavior: When running the command `item modify entity s hotbar.0 {function:"set_ominous_bottle_amplifier",amplifier:10}`, the game should handle out-of-range amplifier values gracefully without crashing. The item modifier should either clamp the amplifier to a valid range or provide an error message, ensuring that the game remains stable and functional after executing the command.
